datum.name: R3 robot datum: carpet plane at the frame centre, +X toward the intake, +Y left, millimetres

objectives.objective: AUTO: start with up to eight supported FUEL and score from a legal launch pose while the HUB is active
objectives.basis: The starting fold holds 37 or more FUEL by free volume (start-capacity premise); the launch and flight cases carry a FUEL into the HUB opening from the 2.7 m pose that the re-run rehearsal credits in AUTO (delivery-pose premise). With Agent FRC 0.84 wait-cycle yield and the shared partner deconfliction, delivering from 2.70 m costs no FUEL: slot 2 credits 124 in both the baseline and R3 series (alliance totals 366 and 382). Pre-0.84 results (96 against 104) were understated by permanent wait cycles.

objectives.objective: Inactive shift: collect and hold the next allocated stock from the DEPOT, OUTPOST or a partner
objectives.basis: The acquire cases take a floor FUEL up the bumper face and over the bumper along the acquisition trial's trace (captured in 0.53 s); the hopper cases follow the entry trial from capture to rest against the stopped flywheel (3.0 s, floor belts stopped). hopper-capacity is 38 or more by free volume. The entry trial is one FUEL in an empty lane: a batch of 24 collected onto stopped belts is not evaluated, and a running belt wedges the FUEL into the stopped pinch (entry-floor-belt-running trials).

objectives.objective: Active shift: carry each FUEL from storage through one transfer into the HUB
objectives.basis: loaded-transit, the launch cases and the flight cases carry the tracked FUEL from its seat into the HUB cavity along the launch and delivery trials' traces. The launch trial backs the FUEL off the stopped wheel, spins the wheel up and feeds it; it releases at 6.86 m/s and 61.9 degrees, and the delivery trials score from 6.70 to 7.00 m/s.

objectives.objective: Active shift: sustain 2.00 FUEL/s to score 24 with stock ready by second 5
objectives.basis: Two pinch lanes. If every FUEL moved at the 0.6 m/s belt speed with 154 mm spacing, each lane would feed 3.9 FUEL/s. The launch trial's single free FUEL rolls on that belt at 0.22 m/s from rest (mean over the feed), which is 1.4 FUEL/s per lane and 2.8 for two lanes against 2.00, so the margin depends on how a stacked batch rides the belt. The launch trial's wheel does 28 J of work per FUEL at the imposed speed. A free 0.006 kg m2 wheel would lose 6.8% of its speed supplying it, against a scoring band of plus or minus 2.2%, so the wheel's inertia or its speed control has to carry the shot (gate G5). The first FUEL of a batch takes 2.3 s from its seat to release (back-off, spin-up, feed). Bulk convergence and the sustained rate are gate G1. Verification gates are in verification-gates.json; the contract assigns physical performance, retention and actuator dynamics to their own commissioned evidence (docs/preliminary-design.md).

objectives.objective: Fallback: score the available batch when supply or traffic consumes the window and return to collecting
objectives.basis: The cycle is piece-count independent; the intake stays deployed in every operating case; the re-run rehearsal keeps the depot loop.

objectives.objective: Traffic: remain in the own zone, keep possession through loaded driving and contact, and yield
objectives.basis: By geometry the front lip stands 61 mm above the floor belts, so by statics a floor FUEL needs about 5.2 g of horizontal deceleration to roll over it; side and rear walls rise above the top layer; the open throat holds no counted FUEL. The seated FUEL is held only by the stopped flywheel behind it and friction: nothing restrains it forward during the loaded transit. Loaded 0.5 g stops are gate G2. Verification gates are in verification-gates.json; the contract assigns physical performance, retention and actuator dynamics to their own commissioned evidence (docs/preliminary-design.md).

objectives.objective: Neutral collector alternative with two field crossings
objectives.basis: The coordinator selected the own-zone role. R3 keeps a BUMP crossing option (bump-crossing premise, 8.7 mm least clearance) with the intake retracted; the re-run TRENCH variant (R3L) credits fewer FUEL than the depot loop.

objectives.objective: End game: Level 1 low-rung hang when its expected 10 points exceed the remaining FUEL service
objectives.basis: Cases reach, seat (2 mm required contact) and lift 70 mm; the 714 mm frame gives 23.9 mm of bumper overlap with each upright (hang-bumper-overlap premise); the hang physics trial at 70.3 kg holds 37.5 mm with the brake and fails without it; its cable load peaks at 1043 N in the lift and settles at 690 N. Jaw capture under lateral offset and the brake hold are gate G3. Verification gates are in verification-gates.json; the contract assigns physical performance, retention and actuator dynamics to their own commissioned evidence (docs/preliminary-design.md).

objectives.objective: AUTO Level 1 TOWER (15 points, two-robot cap)
objectives.basis: The strategy keeps the eight-FUEL AUTO objective; no joined AUTO climb evidence is sought in this layout.

objectives.objective: Reserve the depot entrance and partner lane
objectives.basis: Alliance routing decision owned by the field rehearsal, independent of the robot layout.

objectives.objective: Measurement: observe intake crossing, retained identity, release and downstream crossing on one timebase
objectives.basis: entry sensor at the front lip and pinch sensor at the flywheel lane are placed; the HUB counter is field equipment.
